description.narrative: The proposed Program has the development objective of supporting the implementation of the Strategy for Harmonization of Statistics in Africa 2017 – 2026 (SHaSA2) for Kenya, Rwanda and Tanzania, by strengthening the harmonization, quality, production, timely dissemination and use of core economic and social statistics. SHaSA2 is a continent-wide strategy is anchored in four strategic themes: (1) producing quality statistics for Africa; (2) coordinating the production of quality statistics for Africa; (3) developing sustainable institutional capacities of the African Statistical System (AfSS) and (4) promoting a culture of quality policy and decision-making .The regional Program will improve the quality and harmonization of statistics, produce a core set of economic, social, and sustainability statistics as defined in the International Development Association (IDA)-commitment Data for Policy (D4P). The three countries will use the frameworks and guidelines to produce and disseminate statistics, build statistical capacity with the help of the regional organizations and improve statistical and physical infrastructure while enhancing institutional development. Implemented at the regional level, the operation will close data gaps with harmonized data compliant with international standards contributing to effective policy making and monitoring of progress, regional integration and achievement of global targets. The regional approach will further facilitate coordination among National Statistical Offices (NSOs) by introducing and expanding innovations, peer-to-peer reviewing, and learning, generating positive externalities also beyond the participating countries. The PforR will be structured into three results areas: 1) Harmonization, Quality, Dissemination & Use; 2) Availability & New Data Sources; and 3) Infrastructure & Institutional Development.Results area 1: Harmonization, quality, dissemination & use of statistics. This result area supports activities under Strategic Focus Areas 2 and 4 of the KSDS in Kenya, Pillars 1 and III of the NSDS3 in Rwanda and Component 1 of the TSMP2 in Tanzania. The first Disbursement Linked Indicator (DLI) will improve harmonization and quality of statistics by providing the foundation to enable effective data dissemination by supporting the implementation of regional guidelines according to SHaSA2, extending the data quality and comparability framework at the regional level to include additional data dimensions and developing concepts and frameworks for the integration of new technologies and big data. The second DLI will contribute to statistical literacy and improve dissemination and use of statistics by supporting digital dissemination through online portals and dashboards, inclusion of gender-, disability- and spatially disaggregated statistics as well as improving the timeliness of statistics by using advanced release calendars. Increased use of digital technologies to collect and disseminate statistical information to substitute for paper-based methods can reduce GHG emissions. It also reduces the need for officials and citizens to travel to the statistical offices to obtain statistical reports.Results area 2: Availability & New Data Sources. This result area supports activities under Strategic Focus Area 2 4 of the KSDS in Kenya, Pillars I and II of the NSDS3 in Rwanda and Component 2 of the TSMP2 in Tanzania. The first DLI will produce poverty-, labor- and other socio-economic statistics through household budget and labor force surveys, including data on household vulnerability to climate change. The second DLI will produce enterprise statistics with details on labor demand and productivity while also maintaining a business registry. The third DLI will support agricultural statistics, for example by producing agricultural census information and agricultural productivity statistics, which will allow tracking the use of agricultural inputs to improve crop resilience, the reduction of energy consumption and GHG emissions, as well as climate risks and impacts. The fourth DLI ensures continuous implementation of price statistics feeding into the consumer and producer price indices and will revise and upgrade the System of National Accounts, while improving comparability within the region. The fifth DLI tackles administrative data gaps by integrating ministries and agencies into the national statistical system to harness, complement and improve available data that they gather through routine data collection systems. Finally, the sixth DLI will include the setup of emergency observatories, rapid phone survey deployments and big data analytics to create capacity to monitor and track emerging crises in real-time. This will also generate data sets on climate change impacts and enable better sector planning for climate change adaptation. All results in this area will be produced by incorporating guidelines and frameworks on international standards and regional harmonization. Provisions in the data protection laws in Kenya and Rwanda regarding the right of individuals not to be subject to decisions based on automated processing –including for profiling purposes– are relevant to the Program given the emphasis on the use of new technologies and big data techniques for more advanced statistical analysis and evidence-based policymaking.Results area 3: Infrastructure and Institutional Development. This result area supports activities under Strategic Focus Areas 1 and 3 of the KSDS in Kenya, Pillar III of the NSDS3 in Rwanda and Component 3 of the TSMP2 in Tanzania. The first DLI will upgrade IT infrastructure including the setup of data servers and equipment to implement tablet-surveys while establishing technology to monitor and analyze incoming data on-the-fly. The DLI also includes statistical infrastructure, for example the preparation of sampling frames based on population census and the development of modular data platforms that can form the basis for linking datasets across government such as connecting administrative data to monitoring indicators and the budget. This DLI also enables the program to encourage the adoption of measures that improve energy efficiency, renewable energy deployment, and/or CO2-emission reduction in data centers. The second DLI will enhance institutional capacity and development by building capacity and improving the institutional setup at the regional, national and sub-national level as well as supporting monitoring and evaluation frameworks. Institutional development will include – depending on the implementing agencies needs – analysis and recommendations for improved legal frameworks and stronger mechanisms of institutional oversight to enhance the independence of the agencies, options to mitigate the increasing risk of re-identification from the collection of new forms of personal data including for the use of Big Data analytics, improvements of the management of human resources, organizational and managerial changes, strategic planning as well as improved financial systems. Technology and infrastructure choices will, when possible, take climate change resilience into account. The IPF grants to the AU and the EAC are aligned with DLIs for the PforR, directly supporting achievement of DLIs in all three results areas. Activities under subcomponent 1 of the AU component and sub-component 1.1 of the EAC component develop and provide technical training on the implementation of the reference standards and methods which are measured against DLI 1.1 on the production of harmonized statistics across multiple statistical dimensions. This will also be reflected in improved data quality outputs under results area 2 (DLIs 2.1, 2.2 and 2.4) which require application of relevant international, continental, and regional classifications in the production of data. Activities under sub-component 2 of the AU and subcomponents 3.1 and 3.2 of the EAC IPF components will support countries to achieve

B.1 (b) The Recipient shall recruit or assign, as appropriate and agreed upon with the Association, forPart 2(a) of the Project: (i) a safeguards expert to be based at the PIU within STATAFRIC; (ii) a monitoring and evaluation expertto be based at the PIU within STATAFRIC; (iii) a finance assistant to be based at the PIU within STATAFRIC; (iv) an internalauditor to be based at AU headquarters; and (v) a finance officer to be based at AU headquarters with terms of reference,experience and qualifications satisfactory to the Association, not later than six (6) months from the Effective Date or at a laterdate agreed upon in writing with the Association.

EAC: Schedule 2, Section I. B.2 (b) The recipient shall recruit an additional procurement consultant for the Project ImplementationUnit within the EAC Secretariat, with qualifications and experience and under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association,within six (6) months from the Effective Date.

KEN: Schedule 2, Section I, B.3 (a) The recipient shall establish, by no later than three months after the effectiveness date, andmaintain thereafter, a Program Steering Committee (PSC) to be chaired by the Principal Secretary of the Recipient's Statedepartmentresponsible for Planning, and comprising of the Principal Secretary of the National Treasury, the Director General of theKNBS, and any other members who may be co-opted by the PSC.
